chapter: New York, Dallas and Kansas City
title: Jabbo Smith and the drunk who asked 'What are ya?'
summary: At a dance in Orange, New Jersey, a drunk quizzed Moore about his ancestry and Jabbo Smith teased the man about the guitarist.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: There used to be a band in Newark Jabbo and I used to go to to play with gigs, you know, play around. One time we were playing at the ballroom in Orange, New Jersey and this fella walked---danced by--- he kept looking at me and he kept looking at Jab and looking at the other guy, and he was getting loaded and I'd see him breaking and I'd see him dance by -- he was a white fella -- he'd dance by and he'd stop and look at me again and then go dance by so the next time he danced by he stopped and looked at me straight in the eye and I noticed how loaded -- I'd smell the fumes -- he looked me straight in the eye and says, "What are ya?" I say, "I'm Indian." "From India?" "No, I'm an American Indian." "Oklahoma?" He's loaded now, so I said, "Yes." I wouldn't tell him the truth because I didn't want to be bothered, so Jabbo was sitting next to me in the brass section and he

says, "See that guy next to me over there, the guitar player?" Willie. Willie was awfully dark, he was very, very dark. So he told this white fella, he says, "See that guitar player over there, he's Indian, too." So this fella moved over to where Willie was playing his guitar and looked him straight in the eye and slowly shook his head, "Oh, no, he's not Indian."
I reminded that story to Jabbo Smith the other day. He remembered.
